questions.q: If the coefficients of $x^3 and x^4$ in the expansion of $\left(1+a x+b x^2\right)(1-2 x)^{18}$ in powers of $x$ are both zero, then $(a, b)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
In the expansion of $\left(1+a x+b x^2\right)(1-2 x)^{18}$ coefficient of $x^3 in \left(1+a x+b x^2\right)(1-2 x)^{18}=$ Coefficient of $x^3 in (1-2 x)^{18}+$ coefficient of $x^2 in a(1-2 x)^{18}+$ coefficient of $x in b(1-2 x)^{18}$.
$=-{ }^{18} C_3 \cdot 2^3+a^{18} C_2 \cdot 2^2-b^{18} C_4 \cdot 2\because \quad-{ }^{18} C_3 \cdot 2^3+a^{18} C_2 \cdot 2^2-b^{18} C_4 \cdot 2=0\Rightarrow \frac{18 \times 17 \times 16}{3 \times 2} \cdot 8+a \cdot \frac{18 \times 17}{2} 2^2-b \cdot 18 \cdot 2=0\Rightarrow 17 a-b=\frac{34 \times 16}{3}\ldots$ (i)
Similarly, coefficient of $x^4{ }^{18} C_4 \cdot 2^4-a \cdot{ }^{18} C_3 2^3+b \cdot{ }^{18} C_2 \cdot 2^2=0\therefore \quad 32 a-32 b=240\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$a=16 and b=\frac{272}{3}$

questions.q: The coefficient of the middle term in the binomial expansion in powers of $x$ of $(1+\alpha x)^4$ and $(1-\alpha x)^6$ is the same, if $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The coefficient of the middle term in power of $x(1+\alpha x)^4={ }^4 C_2 \alpha^2$
The coefficient of the middle term in power of $x(1-\alpha x)^6={ }^6 C_3(-\alpha)^3$
According to given condition, $\begin{array}{rlrl} & & { }^4 C_2 \alpha^2 & ={ }^6 C_3(-\alpha)^3 \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{4!}{2!2!} \alpha^2 & =-\frac{6!}{3!3!} \alpha^3 \\ \Rightarrow & 6 \alpha^2 & =-20 \alpha^3 \\ \Rightarrow & & \alpha=-\frac{6}{20} \\ \therefore & & \alpha & =-\frac{3}{10} \end{array}$

questions.solution:
$\because(9)^{50}=(10-1)^{50} \begin{aligned} &=\left[{ }^{50} C_0(10)^{50}(-1)^0-{ }^{50} C_1(10)^{49}(1)\right.+\ldots .]-{ }^{50} C_{49}(10)^1 \\ &+{ }^{50} C_{50}(10)^0\end{aligned} \because$ All the terms in the bracket are multiples of $10^2$.

questions.solution:
Let the coefficient of $x^{-9}$ is in the $(r+1)$ th term in the expansion of $\left(\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{2}{x}\right)^9$, then $\begin{aligned} T_{r+1} & ={ }^9 C_r\left(\frac{x^2}{2}\right)^{9-r}\left(-\frac{2}{x}\right)^r \\ & ={ }^9 C_r \frac{x^{18-2 r}}{2^{9-r}} \cdot \frac{(-1)^r \cdot 2^r}{x^r} \\ & ={ }^9 C_r \frac{x^{18-3 r}}{2^{9-2 r}}(-1)^r \end{aligned}$
For coefficient of $x^{-9}$, put $\begin{aligned} & & x^{18-3 r} & =x^{-9} \\ \Rightarrow & & 18-3 r & =-9 \\ \Rightarrow & & & r \end{aligned}\therefore$ Coefficient of $x^{-9}={ }^9 C_9 \frac{1}{\gamma^{-9}}(-1)^9=-2^9=-512$

questions.solution:

questions.q: The coefficient of the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(\frac{x+1}{x^{2 / 3}-x^{1 / 3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x-x^{1 / 2}}\right)^{10}$ is
questions.solution:
$\frac{x+1}{x^{2 / 3}-x^{1 / 3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x-x^{1 / 2}}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\left(x^{1 / 3}\right)^3+1^3}{x^{2 / 3}-x^{1 / 3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x^{1 / 2}\left(x^{1 / 2}-1\right)} \\ & =\frac{\left(x^{1 / 3}+1\right)\left(x^{2 / 3}-x^{1 / 3}+1\right)}{x^{2 / 3}-x^{1 / 3}+1}-\frac{x^{1 / 2}+1}{x^{1 / 2}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =x^{1 / 3}+1-1-x^{-1 / 2} \\ & =x^{1 / 3}-x^{-1 / 2}\end{aligned}\therefore\left(\frac{x+1}{x^{2 / 3}-x^{1 / 3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x-x^{1 / 2}}\right)^{10}=\left(x^{1 / 3}-x^{-1 / 2}\right)^{10}\begin{aligned} & T_{r+1} \text{$ for $}\left(x^{1 / 3}-x^{-1 / 2}\right) \text{ is } \\ & { }^{10} C_r\left(x^{1 / 3}\right)^{10-r}(-1)^r\left(x^{-1 / 2}\right)^r .\end{aligned}$
For term independent of $x$,
$\frac{10-r}{3}-\frac{r}{2}=0 \begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & 20-2 r-3 r & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & r & =4\end{array} 
Hence, required coefficient $={ }^{10} C_4(-1)^4=210$.$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If there is a term containing x^{2 r} in $\left(x+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^{n-3}$, then
options: $n-2 r$ is a positive integral multiple of 3.
questions.solution:
Suppose $(s+1)$ th term contains $x^{2 r}$.
Then, we have
$\begin{aligned} T_{s+1} & ={ }^{n-3} C_s x^{n-3-s}\left(\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^s \\ & ={ }^{n-3} C_s x^{n-3-3 s}\end{aligned}$
This will contain $x^{2 r}$, if
$n-3-3 s=2 r$\begin{array}{lr}\Rightarrow & s=$\frac{n-3-2 r}{3}$ \\ \Rightarrow & s=$\frac{n-2 r}{3}-$1 \\ \Rightarrow & s+1=$\frac{n-2 r}{3}$ \\ \Rightarrow & n-2 r=3(s+1)\end{array}$
Hence, $(n-2 r)$ is a positive integral multiple of 3.$

Also, the sum of binomial coefficients

$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & 2 S_n=n t_n \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{S_n}{n t_n}=\frac{1}{2}\end{array}$
Now, $\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{S_n}{n t_n}\right)=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}$

questions.q: Given positive integers $r>1, n>2$ and the coefficient of (3r) th and $(r+2)$ th terms in the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{2 n}$ are equal, then
questions.solution:
$3 r$ th term in the expansion of $(1+x)^{2 n}=\binom{2 \pi}{3 r-1} x^{3 r-1}$
and $(r+2)$ th term in the expansion of $(1+x)^{2 n}=\binom{2 n}{r+1} x^{r+1}$
Given that the binomial coefficients of (3r)th and $(r+2)$ th terms are equal.
$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & \binom{2 n}{3 r-1}=\binom{2 n}{r+1} \\
\Rightarrow & 3 r-1=r+1 \\
\text{ or } & 2 n=(3 r-1)+(r+1) \\
\Rightarrow & 2 r=2 \quad \text{ or } \quad 2 n=4 r \\
\Rightarrow & r=1 \quad \text{or} \quad n=2 r \\
\text{ But } & r>1 \\
\therefore & n=2 r
\end{array}$
